function: Channel prediction: an LLM forecasts future delay–Doppler channel coefficients of an OTFS satellite downlink with a fluid-antenna receiver from past frames (pp. 1, 6).
system: Satellite UPA (Nt elements, half-wavelength) to one fluid antenna with Np ports and one RF chain; OTFS, LEO; no RIS; band not stated (pp. 3, 8).
method: Pretrained LLaMA-3-1B fine-tuned with LoRA (rank 8) by supervised NMSE regression (AdamW, 100 epochs, batch 64) on PCA-compressed delay–Doppler channel codes (pp. 5–7).
data_channel: Own simulated narrowband Ricean delay–Doppler channel with Bessel-correlated ports; taps 'typically drawn' from an unnamed 3GPP profile; no public dataset or measurements (pp. 3–4, 7).
test_conditions: One simulated dataset, train/test split not described; past window 50, horizons 10–50, SNR sweep; no new scenario, band, or configuration tested (pp. 7–10).
baselines: Learned only: LSTM, GRU, Transformer, GPT-2 (p. 7); perfect-CSI 'Actual Channel' reference (pp. 9–10); no non-learned predictor, although the introduction cites a Kalman-RNN (p. 3).
metrics: NMSE (dB) and RMSE of predicted channel; ergodic capacity versus SNR and outage probability versus target rate from predicted versus actual channel (pp. 7–10).
complexity: Partial: input cut over 99%, 50–100 PCA coefficients versus about 8000 (pp. 3, 5); reconstruction costs one complex multiplication per port (p. 5); no FLOPs, LoRA parameters, or runtime.
q1_support: p. 3: "a narrowband Ricean channel comprising a deterministic line-of-sight (LoS) path and P scattered multipath components". Taps are only "typically drawn" from a generic "3GPP delay–Doppler tap profile" (p. 4); no TR or profile is named and Section IV lists no channel parameters.
q2_support: p. 7: "the future prediction lengths vary as M ∈ {10, 20, 30, 40, 50}". Only the horizon and the capacity SNR sweep (p. 10) vary; no scenario, band, antenna, or Doppler setting outside training is tested.
q3_support: p. 9: "four baselines (GRU, LSTM, GPT-2, Transformer)". All four are learned networks and the Actual Channel is a perfect-CSI reference, so no non-learned baseline exists; the Kalman-RNN announced on p. 3 is never evaluated.
q4_support: p. 5: "a single complex multiplication per receive port" costs only the phase-ramp reconstruction step; no FLOPs, trainable-parameter count, or runtime of the LLM predictor is given (p. 7 gives only LLaMA-3-1B and LoRA r = 8).
q5_support: p. 7: "This section details the simulation dataset". The channel data are self-simulated, and no link to code or data appears anywhere in the paper.
notes: The PDF is the arXiv v1 preprint (arXiv:2505.09751v1) and prints no DOI, so the DOI-to-title match cannot be checked from the text. Area: delay–Doppler channel prediction fits area 2 by function and area 4 by OTFS; the tie-break gives 4 (area 6 does not apply, since no resource, power, or beam control is learned). RIS appears only in related work (p. 2) and in a passing remark on RIS phase updates (p. 8). Borderline marks: q1 (the 3GPP reference is hedged and unnamed) and q4 (one-step operation count only). The contributions (p. 3) claim learned port selection and a Kalman-RNN comparison, but the reference port is fixed to n_p = 1 by convention (p. 4) and only LSTM, GRU, Transformer, and GPT-2 are evaluated.
